name: File upload
description: A control for choosing one or more files from the device to send with a form, built on <input type="file">. It can add a drop zone for dragged files and a list of the files chosen.
summary: Choose files from the device to send

elements.name: Label
elements.description: Visible <label> that says what to upload

elements.name: Hint text
elements.description: Allowed file types and the size limit

elements.name: Drop zone
elements.description: Area that accepts dragged files, around the button

elements.name: File list
elements.description: Chosen files with name, size or progress, and a remove button

usageNotes: Keep the native <input type="file"> underneath any custom design. It already works with keyboards, screen readers and mobile file choosers.
Dragging must never be the only way to add a file. Always include a button that opens the file chooser (WCAG 2.5.7).
State the allowed file types and size limit in the hint before people choose, and set accept to match. Check files on the server as well.
When a file is rejected, name the file and the reason in the error message, such as "report.exe is not an allowed file type", and keep the other files.
Tell screen reader users about upload progress and completion, for example with a Progress bar and a polite live region.
htmlOutline:
<label for="cv">Upload your CV</label>
<input id="cv" type="file" name="cv" accept=".pdf,.docx">
